checks.per_tenant_checks_stand_alone: PASS, with one documented residual edge case. Tests 1/3/4 (ISS-0332): pre/post Registry.get_type/2 assertions scoped to the test's own tenant_id directly observe schema_version transition (or non-transition). A 'wrongly updated' or 'wrongly not-updated' bug flips this state and fails the assertion independent of the (now loosened) global tally -- robust to DB pollution by construction. Test 2 (ISS-0343): the 'run doesn't crash' property is proven by reaching the {:ok, %{...}} shape match at all (not a count), and 'healthy tenant still updated despite vanished tenant' is proven by its own scoped post-run check -- both robust to stray rows. The added standalone Registry.register_type/2 call against vanished_tenant_id is weaker evidence (confirms the error condition still holds, not that Backfill.run/1 itself routed that tenant to :skipped), but the properties this test regression-guards (no crash; healthy tenant unaffected) do not depend on it. Residual gap noted, not blocking: for tests 3/4, a hypothetical bug that evaluates correctly and leaves DB state genuinely unchanged but fails to increment the skipped tally would be caught by neither the per-tenant state check (state is genuinely unchanged) nor the lower bound (maskable by stray rows). This is a pure tally-accounting bug with no functional/state impact -- not the class of regression ISS-0332/ISS-0343 or this fix target -- so it does not undermine the design's core claim that per-tenant checks are the real regression proof.
